actual_scope: Independently audit PR5369 PROOF.md §6 and reversible_cnf.py: complete dirty controlled swap, chronological Boolean compiler, actual source-emitted five-role endpoints, instruction and exact-bit bounds.
scope_change_reason: Handoff-first override of one picker run (bit-mechanisms; seed aa32479c3ec3e4781cbe692d0b861686). PR5521 explicitly leaves this proof/source implication open. Use formal-interface-lemma for a scoped mathematical audit before any formalization; no reroll or new cutoff campaign.
bottleneck_link: The native identity checker has a claimed complexity boundary even for reversible dirty programs. A source-bound independent reduction audit checks whether that boundary is valid and clarifies why finite solver limits or small-width samples cannot imply a general efficient checker; no physical supplier cost follows.
stop_rule: Stop after the explicit §6 compiler/equivalence/size audit and bounded independent rational controls. Do not rerun the general source verifier, extend tensor cutoffs, claim a new hardness theorem, or start physical supplier/Lean/cold-admission work.

open_questions.question: Does the general native endpoint compiler preserve its declared grammar and complete dirty state at an actual source-bound caller?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This audit covers only the commuting-sign CNF reduction, not arbitrary affine/quadratic native maps or the source solver implementation.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one unclaimed concrete caller and pin the generator composition/inversion, self-query conventions, independent inputs and required returns; compare emitted endpoints with a separate literal interpreter.
open_questions.blocked_by: A named caller and its full source closure; the present sign reduction supplies neither physical execution nor general compiler acceptance.

open_questions.question: Can a practically useful tractable subclass of the native identity problem be isolated without changing the dirty-input contract?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The general coNP classification does not rule out efficient algorithms for a bounded or structurally restricted caller family.
open_questions.first_step: Name a concrete caller restriction, such as a fixed generator-support or role-interaction structure, and prove the resulting exact decision cost while preserving all returns.
open_questions.blocked_by: A useful actual caller restriction and full encoding/budget; finite solver samples alone do not provide such a theorem.
